description: Local, long distance, and interconnected VoIP calling for about 74,000 lines, including 911 call origination, STIR/SHAKEN signing, and SS7 signaling
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: 911 calling must not be lost; PSAP notice within 30 minutes and NORS notification within 120 minutes (wireline) of a qualifying outage; RPO is the age of the last nightly element configuration backup
manual_workaround: Fail VoIP to the CO-4 softswitch node and SBCs; TDM lines are unaffected unless their host switch fails; 911 calls from affected lines route through the surviving node
dependent_third_parties: SS7 hub provider; state NG911 system service provider; upstream transit providers; STI certificate authority
dependent_people_or_facilities: NOC (24x7); voice engineers; CO-1 and CO-4 facilities and power
quantified_operational_impact: About 74,000 lines; at the busy hour about 9,000 calls in progress; each hour down affects about 30,000 call attempts
quantified_regulatory_impact: Missed PSAP or NORS clocks are FCC enforcement matters (47 CFR 4.9(f)-(h)); calls without STIR/SHAKEN signing may be labeled or blocked downstream
public_safety_impact: Severe: 911 calls fail for affected lines

description: 14 legacy 911 circuit pairs and administrative lines whose last service-provider facility is CO-1, CO-3, CO-5, CO-6, or CO-8, serving 7 PSAPs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A PSAP that loses its 911 trunks cannot receive emergency calls; 47 CFR 9.19 requires physical diversity, 24 hours of backup power at full office load, and diverse monitoring for these facilities
manual_workaround: State NG911 system service provider re-routes calls to a backup PSAP; diverse circuit of each pair carries traffic; field crews dispatched with priority
dependent_third_parties: State NG911 system service provider; PSAPs; utility power
dependent_people_or_facilities: NOC; outside plant crews; CO-1, CO-3, CO-5, CO-6, CO-8 power plants
quantified_operational_impact: 7 PSAPs serving parts of 11 counties; 2 of 14 circuit pairs share a fiber segment (single point of failure)
quantified_regulatory_impact: Covered 911 service provider duties (47 CFR 9.19(b), (c)); PSAP notification (4.9(h)); 911 Authorities may request reliability certifications (9.20(d))
public_safety_impact: Severe: emergency calls in a county cannot be answered locally

description: Fiber and DSL internet access for about 197,000 subscribers, including DNS and DHCP
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $411,000 residential broadband revenue per day; outages drive care call surges; many customers use broadband for VoIP and 911 calling; transport outages can meet the 667 OC3-minute NORS test
manual_workaround: Restore element configurations from backups; reroute around failed rings; status page and outbound messages
dependent_third_parties: Upstream transit providers; DDoS scrubbing provider
quantified_operational_impact: A 4-hour area-wide outage affects up to 197,000 subscribers and triples inbound care calls
quantified_regulatory_impact: NORS reporting for transport outages meeting 4.9(f)(2); state consumer complaints
public_safety_impact: Moderate: customers who rely on VoIP over broadband for 911 lose it

business_process: Network monitoring, outage response, and regulatory outage reporting
description: 24x7 NOC detects outages, dispatches crews, notifies PSAPs, files NORS and DIRS reports
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The 30-minute PSAP notification clock runs from discovery; the NOC must be working within 30 minutes of losing CO-1
manual_workaround: Move to the secondary NOC at CO-4 (staffed within 30 minutes); printed PSAP contact lists; NORS filed from any internet connection
dependent_third_parties: FCC NORS and DIRS portals; PSAP contacts
dependent_people_or_facilities: 48 NOC staff; CO-1 and CO-4 NOC rooms
quantified_operational_impact: Without the NOC, outages are found by customer calls, adding 30 to 90 minutes to detection
quantified_regulatory_impact: PSAP notice within 30 minutes (4.9(h)(4)); NORS notification within 120 minutes for wireline (4.9(f)); DIRS daily reports when activated (4.18)
public_safety_impact: Severe: PSAPs are not warned of 911 outages

business_process: Business data services (dedicated internet, Ethernet, wholesale backhaul)
description: Protected circuits for 3,400 business and government sites and backhaul for wireless carriers under a 99.99% SLA
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $197,000 revenue per day; SLA credits of 10% to 25% of monthly charges after 4 hours; wholesale backhaul outages take down other carriers' cell sites
manual_workaround: Protected paths switch automatically; manual reroute through alternate rings; priority dispatch for government and hospital circuits
dependent_third_parties: Upstream transit providers; wireless carrier customers
quantified_operational_impact: 3,400 sites; 112 cell site backhaul circuits; a county government and a hospital system depend on protected circuits
quantified_regulatory_impact: Transport outages can meet the 667 OC3-minute NORS test (4.9(f)(2)); contract SLA reporting
public_safety_impact: Moderate: hospital and county government connectivity degraded

description: Hosted PBX for about 600 business customers (14,200 seats) on the cluster in the CO-1 data hall, including their 911 calling
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: 99.99% SLA; customers include a hospital system and county offices that place 911 calls through the platform; call routing configurations change many times a day, so the RPO is 15 minutes
manual_workaround: Fail over to the standby cluster node; forward main numbers to mobile phones through the customer portal; emergency call routing kept on the softswitch
dependent_third_parties: Hosted voice software vendor; colocation power and cooling vendors
dependent_people_or_facilities: Business Services engineers; CO-1 data hall
quantified_operational_impact: 14,200 seats; 600 customers; about 160,000 calls per business day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Interconnected VoIP outage reporting (4.9(g)); PSAP notice if 911 calling is affected (4.9(h)); SOC 2 availability commitment
public_safety_impact: Severe: 911 calling from customer sites fails

description: Configuration, monitoring, and change service for about 1,900 customer edge devices through a vendor SaaS orchestrator
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customer edges keep forwarding traffic without the orchestrator; changes and monitoring stop; SLA credits after 8 hours
manual_workaround: Direct device console access through the jump hosts for urgent changes; manual monitoring of critical customers
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,900 managed edges; about 40 change requests per business day

description: Receive and implement court-ordered intercepts through the TTP; keep intercept records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Active intercepts must not lapse and must be activated only with lawful authorization (47 U.S.C. 1004; 47 CFR 1.20003-1.20004); records RPO 24 hours
manual_workaround: TTP re-provisions from its order records; the 4 authorized employees re-activate intercepts manually
quantified_operational_impact: About 30 orders a year; typically 2 to 4 active at a time
quantified_regulatory_impact: Lapsed or compromised intercepts must be reported to law enforcement (1.20003(c))
public_safety_impact: Moderate: investigations of serious crime delayed

description: Phone, chat, chatbot, and retail account support, including authentication before CPNI disclosure
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Outages create call surges; agents must authenticate callers before releasing call detail (47 CFR 64.2010(b)); about 9,500 contacts per day
manual_workaround: Callback queue; offline account report refreshed hourly; status page and outbound messages; chatbot in outage-message mode
dependent_third_parties: BSS vendor; CCaaS vendor; chatbot vendor; overflow call center vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: 140 care agents; 35 overflow agents; CO-1 care center
quantified_operational_impact: About 9,500 contacts per day; a full day down adds about 4,000 callbacks and loses about 120 sales orders
quantified_regulatory_impact: CPNI authentication must hold during workarounds (64.2010); no call detail by phone without the password

description: Sales, payments, equipment swaps, and in-person account service at 3 stores
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers can use phone and portal; photo ID check needed before in-store CPNI access (64.2010(d))
manual_workaround: Take payments through the processor's mobile terminal; paper equipment log
quantified_regulatory_impact: In-store CPNI access only after photo ID (64.2010(d))

description: Orders, number porting, line and broadband activation, and Business Services turn-ups
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 450 installs and changes per business day; port requests have carrier deadlines
manual_workaround: Paper work orders; manual activation by network engineers for priority orders
quantified_operational_impact: About 450 orders per day deferred; port-in deadlines missed after 24 hours
quantified_regulatory_impact: Number porting timelines (FCC rules, not analyzed here)

description: Trouble tickets, crew dispatch, and outside plant repair, including storm restoration
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Repairs for 911 circuits and protected business circuits cannot wait; about 700 tickets per day in storms
manual_workaround: Phone dispatch from the NOC; paper tickets; crews work from printed outage maps
quantified_operational_impact: About 300 tickets per normal day, 700 in storms

description: Collect and rate CDRs, bill about 205,000 accounts (6,800 on the legacy CLEC system), take payments
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Switches buffer CDRs for 72 hours, after which toll records are lost; billing runs in cycles, so short outages delay cash rather than lose it
manual_workaround: Hold bill cycles; extend switch CDR buffers where possible; payments through the processor continue
dependent_third_parties: BSS vendor; bill print vendor; payment processor
quantified_operational_impact: About $871,000 of billing per day; a 5-day outage delays about $4.2 million of cash and loses about $60,000 of unrecoverable toll revenue if CDRs overflow
quantified_regulatory_impact: CDRs are CPNI; lost or altered records create disputes

description: Campaigns that use CPNI, the churn prediction model, opt-out notices, and the campaign register
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No customer service depends on it; approval records must be kept at least 1 year (64.2007(a)(3), 64.2009(c))
manual_workaround: Pause campaigns; no CPNI-based marketing until approval flags can be checked
quantified_regulatory_impact: Using CPNI without approval is a CPNI rule violation (64.2007(b))

business_process: Regulatory filings and robocall traceback response
description: NORS final reports, CPNI certification, RMD updates, traceback responses within 24 hours, CALEA filings, 911 reliability records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Traceback requests must be answered within 24 hours (64.6305(a)(2)); RMD updates within 10 business days (64.6305(d)(5))
manual_workaround: Answer tracebacks from CDR queries run by the NOC; file through FCC web portals from any device
dependent_third_parties: FCC portals; industry traceback consortium; regulatory counsel
quantified_operational_impact: About 18 traceback requests a year; filings cluster in March (CPNI, Secure Networks Act) and after outages
quantified_regulatory_impact: Missed traceback or RMD duties can lead to removal from the RMD, after which other providers must not accept the company's calls

description: Payroll for 850 employees, HR records, general ledger, payables
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs every 2 weeks; missing a payroll is the main harm
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll; manual payables for critical vendors
